utterances.text: There are going to be further changes, are there, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, because for formality sake, I think -- anyway, I have no problems with having it --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, no, Your Honour. We can certainly wait. That was going to be my next question. For obvious reasons, one of Your Honour's rulings has caused some interest, can I put it that way, and we were wondering when we were likely to get the written decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, I checked yesterday. I would say pretty soon, but I can't give you the date, because it's in the process of being collated together, and then it goes to the Senior Legal Officer to check before it's given to me, and then obviously we have to check it again amongst ourselves. It's a process which takes its time, as you know. But all the staff is working on it and the latest information that I got yesterday, first thing as the week started, as, of course, as you can imagine: Where do we stand?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's -- I just wondered if Your Honours had an idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Also because I wanted to retain, maintain the deadline that we had indicated, or the estimate date that we had indicated some time back as being the date when the written decision was to be expected.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the final two matters, which are much shorter: Firstly, Your Honour, we discovered that we were right, that the -- Kelly Philpott has kindly checked over the break, and that exhibit was under seal. We had it marked. The Registry didn't. Now, my concern is that if this happens again, an exhibit which should be truly under seal, if it's not apparent on the Registry markings, can suddenly go into public thing. So I'm asking if perhaps the Registry check that they have probably marked all exhibits under seal which should be under seal. And Your Honour, the final matter is this: Your Honours raised the question of whether Mr. Brdjanin would be testifying and asked for information when we met again. I don't think we've covered that one yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. But I also -- anyway. Mr. Ackerman, let's start with the list first, because when I saw this list yesterday, I understood, even though it said exhibit list, submission number 1, that we were having a list of documents that were going to be made use of in the course of the testimony of this witness. I'm obviously wrong, in the sense that you meant it to be the first phase of the exhibit list that we referred to earlier on. When are we going to have the pleasure of the complete list, at least interim? I understand that as we go along there will be, as was the case with the Prosecution, new exhibits coming to light. I don't expect you to have those included now if you don't know about them. But all those documents that you know about and that you intend to tender, I think it's about time that we have a compilation of them. Perhaps you can, instead of forcing my hands to place an order, tell me when to expect this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I can tell you what's happening. My first priority is to get witnesses into this courtroom and prepared to keep the trial going. My second priority is developing an exhibit list. That's what I do when I have any time at all besides working on witnesses. What you see is what is the spreadsheet on my computer that is the Defence Exhibit list. Yesterday I had about three hours, I think, to spend, and I think I may have added another 15 or 20 documents. I haven't looked lately, but I've added some documents to that list. As soon as I get them properly marked and everything, then they will be brought here and an updated list will be provided. But the only way to do that that I can possibly think of is on a rolling basis, Your Honour, because I have to silt and look through a large quantity of documents and make a decision as to whether I intend to use them as exhibits or not. I have a lot that I know I'm not going to use as exhibits but I do have to go through that process having gone through the witness interviews very recently in Banja Luka. I now know what our witnesses basically are able to do and therefore what documents -- find the documents that I think will assist them in that. So I'm just working through it as fast as I can and I assure you that I will use all available moments, and that's my second priority as to what needs to be done here. If I had a larger staff, I might be able to do it a lot quicker, but I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll discuss it amongst ourselves and then we'll take a decision accordingly. The second point, Ms. Korner, help me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the second point that I made was in respect of -- well, this business of -- it's linked, about the sudden production last night of exhibits, which clearly should have been disclosed a long time ago. And when this witness was seen and interviewed and said he had these documents, that's when they should have been obtained. But, Your Honour, it's the same point, and I'll leave -- witness number 2, Your Honour, and that was really a request rather than --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Witness number 2, I take it, because I -- you have more or less confused me now. I will tell you what I understood was going to happen. Originally, for the week starting on the 27th of October, we were told that there was going to be Witness number 6, to be followed by Witness number 2, and then in the following week, starting on the 3rd of November, the week which start -- dedicating the first two days to the examination of the military expert. I was then told by Ms. Sutherland, either yesterday or on Friday - I don't remember exactly when - that the military expert cross-examination was going to be shifted to the week starting on the 27th of October, which to me meant shifting the evidence of Witness number 6 to some other day. And I was taking it for granted that Witness number 2 would still be coming for the last three days of that week, the week starting on the 27th.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. That's not what we've been told, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If that's not the position, I think we need to know exactly who is coming when, at least for the next two weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I want to have the same rule that you had for the Prosecutor. On every Thursday I'll tell the Prosecutor who is coming next week. That's what you had them do. They always did that to us. And I want the same rule. So on Thursday I'll tell them who is coming next week. They know that I will be cross-examining Mr. Brown on Monday, and they also already know that Boro Blagojevic is also coming. Beyond that I don't think I have to tell them. I gave them a list of our witnesses and the general order we're going to call them. That's what they've done with us. And I want the Thursday rule like they had.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are two matters. One is that the Thursday rule was just a confirmation of what was on the list and people were going backwards because people were taking longer. We gave a list in advance, and particularly of major witnesses. Now, Your Honour will recall that one of the reasons that Mr. Treanor and Mr. Brown have to come back now is that Mr. Ackerman said that he was unable to be prepared to cross-examine those witnesses. I can't now remember the reasons. I think because they came -- at that stage we were piling in the rest of our witnesses. But we need proper notice of major witnesses. Radic is a major witness. We therefore need to know, in advance, not the Thursday before the Monday, when he is coming. The same applies to major members of the ARK Crisis Staff who at present are listed as witnesses. The reason being is that we are preparing the same way as Mr. Ackerman and Mr. Cunningham for cross-examination, by dividing up witnesses. If we're suddenly told that a major witness, who, as I say, we have binders of information on, is going to be appearing on the Monday and we're told that on the Thursday, that's a trick to catch us out, if you like, and it's not good enough. So, Your Honour, I'm just -- I don't want an order at this moment, but I'm just -- I'm saying so that Your Honours know the situation, and Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, if you want to impose a different rule on me than you imposed on the Prosecutor, go ahead, but I think it's decidedly unfair if you do that. Ms. Korner's representations to the contrary. They frequently on Thursday gave us witnesses that we had no idea were coming until that moment. And so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, let's deal with it in a different manner. I would like you, since there is a change in the schedule as submitted to us in the first place, and since it is not clear to me as to who will follow Mr. Brown on week 2, that is, in the week starting on the 27th of October, I would like you, Mr. Ackerman, by tomorrow, or by Thursday morning, to resubmit the list of the witnesses we are expected to hear in week 2, week 3, and week 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So you are going to impose a different rule. You never made them do that, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was asking from time to time the Prosecution to give us a list of the witnesses and it was an ever-changing list, as you are fully aware, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we supplied --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Being changed from day to day.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We can produce -- that we supply full lines of municipality witnesses which were adjusted when things went wrong, but that was well in advance of the witnesses coming and that's all that Mr. Ackerman --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've given them a full list of witnesses through December. They have it through December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And this is why you have no need to complain, Mr. Ackerman, because what I am telling you is there is obviously going to be a change in week 2. There is going to be a change in week 3, and I don't know if, as a consequence of that, we are expected to have a change in week 4. I'm asking you to review these three weeks and come back to us with a replacement if necessary or a confirmation of the order of witnesses that you had planned for these three weeks starting from the 27th of October.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And Your Honour can I just mention, he added confusion. According to this list we got, witnesses week 5, witness number 29, 25th -- two days. If you turn over the page you will see the same witness in the 1st of December, but reduced to one day. So I'm not quite clear what's happening there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know if it's the same one or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It is. It's the same number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It is, and that one's been removed from our list. Well, it wasn't supposed to be given to you. I've given you what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, let's not quarrel about this. We require to know as well. It's not a question of the Prosecution. I mean, it's a simple exercise. If you that I number 2 is going to be coming over in week 4 instead of week 2, or if you don't know, you just say I don't know. But in the meantime, we want to know who is going to take his place in the week starting on the 27th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I'm trying to answer you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So work on it, and Thursday morning, please come back with a revised --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm going to answer you right now. Now that you have imposed a different rule on me, I will respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not imposing. I'm asking you to address the same list that you have to tell us what the changes are.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: On Monday, 27 October, I believe we're having Mr. Brown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The only change in the witness order on account of that will be that number 8, Milorad Sajic, will be moved probably to January. Otherwise, the order stays the same. I think that answers everybody's questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, it doesn't answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because if we are moving Mr. Brown to the week of the 27th October, and that cross-examination is expected to last two days, then we can't possibly have in the same week witness number 6 and Witness number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I just said the order remains the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Brown will be followed by Boro Blagojevic, who will be followed by Predrag Radic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Your Honour, that's just what -- when -- I'm sorry to repeat out of Court conversations, but Mr. Ackerman was spoken to, not by myself, but by another one of the lawyers, he informed us that Mr. Radic could not come. It was not known when Mr. Radic was going to come. And now suddenly we're told that he's coming, that we have to have a little bit more certainty than that. We understood that Sajic was going to be following on effectively, because Brown was moved up so Sajic was moved up. Now we're told he's going to January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Ms. Korner. Do I have the indulgence of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the interpreters and the technicians to have another five minutes, sit for another five minutes? Okay. I thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, Your Honour. I'm asking for Your Honours to make an order. I want a revised witness list for Christmas. This is clearly what we got now is now so confused, I would like an order that we get a revised witness list by tomorrow morning, until the Christmas break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it that you intend to stick to the cross-examination of Mr. Brown on the -- starting on Monday, the 27th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's one change in the list. Mr. Brown got moved up to the 27th. That moved everybody else down except for Milorad Sajic, who I moved to January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's the only change.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Korner takes that as a surprise and in contradiction of what supposedly was exchanged between you outside the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We were ask to put him forward because Radic couldn't come. It has got nothing to do with us. We said yes because we want to assist on this and we said we were quite happy to do that. That's why I raised when is Radic coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That was true, Your Honour. He couldn't come during the week of October 27th. That's all. It wasn't that he couldn't ever come.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I take it that he will be coming in the week following, because if Brown takes two days and Blagojevic takes two to three days, that's the full -- the entire week of the 27th October.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: He follows Blagojevic whenever that happens to come. And I'm not sure when that's going to be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So then presumably Mr. Radic will -- is to be expected in the week starting on the 3rd. That's how I understand it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt. I know it's killing the LiveNote. Please can I have an order that let's not have this to and from discussion, that tomorrow morning we get a revised witness list because we have also included witness for the ten days that Mr. Ackerman has asked to have off and it came as news to us that Mr. Sajic was not going to be here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I object very strongly to any kind of an order like that because it would be totally different treatment than what you ordered with the Prosecutor. It would just be unfair.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, I don't think it's a case that we give an order. We've never given any such orders. What we are making clear is that the understanding is that Mr. Brown will commence -- the cross-examination of Mr. Brown will commence on the 27th of October, and that it's expected to last two days. Mr. Brown will be followed by the testimony of-- why -- I can mention the name Boro Blagojevic, which is expect to last two to three days, and that should take, therefore, the entire week, starting on the 27th of October. And that the testimony of Mr. Radic, according to what Mr. Ackerman is saying, will commence on Monday, the 3rd of November.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, that's -- if Your Honour won't make the order, but I would have thought Your Honours would have liked to know -- Your Honours have made orders before, and Your Honours -- I should -- my submission is that Mr. Ackerman's bleat of this is unfair is nonsense. This is -- He knows what the witnesses are likely to be. But, however, if Your Honours won't make the order --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thought you were satisfied with what has been stated, I mean, for the time being at least. Now, if there is a change, then obviously we will change too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I make it absolutely clear that they need not bring -- if Radic is going to start on Monday, the 3rd of November, he's going to take the whole week; in fact, probably longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm fully aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So let's stop there, for the time being, because the next witness would be Milorad Sajic, and you said that he won't be coming here before January.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Not before January. The following -- following, Predrag Radic, will be number 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I ask, at least on a counsel-to-counsel basis, instead of just announcing this today, which is the first time we've heard it: We've got somebody preparing for Sajic. Your Honour, that's why I say: This stop/start is not good enough. I appreciate we did have problems. That's what Mr. Ackerman refers to. And we confirmed the following week. But the list of potential witnesses was notified well in advance, and as soon as we knew that there was a problem, we informed the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I wouldn't be surprised if this changes again, and I wouldn't be surprised if some of the witnesses that you have here eventually will decide not to come forward, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And, Your Honours, what about Mr. Brdjanin? Are we going to be told whether he's going to testify at some stage or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, and that is the last. Do I take it that your client is not testifying, Mr. Ackerman, at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's not the last matter, and no decision has been made about that. But I am very upset by another matter that is raised by Ms. Korner today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which is what?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Which is: Throughout the Prosecution's case, witnesses would show up with diaries, with documents, with all kinds of things, and the Prosecutor would say: Gee, Judge, we didn't know about them until they came here with them, and please excuse us. And I never once stood up and accused them of being dishonest about that, not once. And the first time one of our witnesses comes with documents that we didn't know he was bringing, she gets up and accuses us of dishonesty, that we must have known about them a long time and just withheld them intentionally. And I resent that greatly, because it's not true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't worry about it, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It's outrageous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Don't worry about it, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I didn't -- I'm not suggesting Mr. Ackerman did this intentionally. What I'm suggesting is that when his investigator, or Mr. Ackerman, or Mr. Cunningham, saw this witness, it was clear he was going to talk about this from the summary, that is the stage at which the document should have been collected. But I'm not accusing Mr. Ackerman of dishonesty.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's exactly what she was doing, and I tell you, as an officer of this Court, that we had no idea he was bringing these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I take your word, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: We had asked him to see if he could find some documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I take it that everyone knows exactly what his or her responsibilities are, and that as soon as documents become available, you will make them available too, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we didn't just do it, you know, at our leisure. We got the CLSS to process them in less than a day. It's not like we were dragging our feet about them. And I just really resent Ms. Korner's accusations in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We stand adjourned until tomorrow morning at 9.00, and then please do remember that we will continue again in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
